description:
memory.rs:470-544 implements query_objects with only one filter path ('inTaskList') and no sort handling. RFC 8620 §5.5 requires that an unsupported sort or filter produces 'unsupportedSort' / 'unsupportedFilter' SetErrors at the method-level. Two concrete consequences:

1. (Spec deviation) A Task/query with sort=[{property: 'due', isAscending: true}] returns ids in Id-string lexicographic order, silently — a client sorting by due-date sees ids ordered by id-creation-order and likely concludes 'sort works' (because for the deterministic 'task<n:016x>' demo ids, creation order is monotonic by id). Tests cannot easily detect this because the integration test fixture uses sequential creation and never asserts a non-id-order sort property.

2. (Maintainer burden) A consumer copying this method's shape into their own backend gets the wrong invariant teaching: 'sort can be ignored' is the implicit lesson. Production backends MUST validate sort/filter against the type's QueryObject::supported_sort / supported_filter sets and return unsupportedSort/Filter.

Recommended remediation: (a) add a rustdoc on query_objects explaining that the implementation is filter-and-sort-blind by design, and that a production backend MUST inspect both arguments; (b) when sort is non-None and contains a property other than 'id', return Err(MemoryError) wrapped in serverFail — making the missing functionality loud rather than silent. Alternative: implement a minimal sort by 'due' / 'created' / 'updated' on the Task store for fidelity with the integration-test fixture set. The choice is a judgement call.
title: MemoryBackend.query_objects silently ignores sort and filter
